title: Italy: Constitutional Intergenerational Equity
executive_summary: Italy's intergenerational equity model is a three-layer stack: (1) constitutional entrenchment via Constitutional Law 1/2022 (Articles 9 and 41), naming future generations and environmental limits on economic activity; (2) administrative operationalisation through Generational Impact Assessment (VIG) in Law 167/2025, integrated into regulatory impact analysis for government bills; and (3) judicial enforcement through Constitutional Court doctrine on equità intergenerazionale, spanning public finance (from 2019) and environment (especially post-2022). Italy does not have a Wales-style Future Generations Commissioner, but it is among the few states that constitutionally name future generations alongside environment and biodiversity. As of mid-2026, VIG is legally binding but the implementing DPCM and Observatory are still being stood up, while municipalities (Parma, Bologna) already run local VIG ahead of central government practice.

layers.label: Constitutional foundation
layers.role: Binds legislature, executive, and courts; elevates future generations from policy language to fundamental principles.

layers.label: Statutory operationalisation
layers.role: VIG in AIR for government normative acts; National Observatory at Presidency of the Council of Ministers.

layers.label: Judicial doctrine
layers.role: Equità intergenerazionale as legitimacy parameter in fiscal discipline and environmental derogations.

constitutional_reform.significance: First amendment to Italy's fundamental principles since 1948; promoted by ASviS from 2016; passed with near-unanimous parliamentary support.

articles.text_en: The Republic protects the environment, biodiversity and ecosystems, also in the interest of future generations. State law regulates the ways and forms of animal protection.
articles.text_it: La Repubblica tutela l'ambiente, la biodiversità e gli ecosistemi, anche nell'interesse delle future generazioni. La legge dello Stato disciplina i modi e le forme della tutela degli animali.

articles.text_en: Private economic initiative is free. It may not be carried out in contrast with social utility or in such a way as to damage health, the environment, security, freedom, or human dignity.
Law determines programmes and controls so that public and private economic activity may be directed and coordinated to social and environmental purposes.

what_italy_lacks: No standalone Future Generations Commissioner or Well-being of Future Generations Act (unlike Wales)
No freestanding constitutional right to a healthy environment as a single justiciable right — protection is framed through Article 9 duties and administrative/civil routes
VIG applies to government rulemaking, not Parliament's primary legislation in the same way

jurisprudence.overview: Before the 2022 reform, the Constitutional Court developed equità intergenerazionale as a cross-cutting legitimacy test, especially in public finance. After 2022, environmental cases explicitly cite Article 9's future-generations language.

streams.label: Public finance and debt
streams.summary: Structural deficit prolongation and dilated debt-repayment timelines that shift burdens onto future cohorts without correlated benefits violate Articles 81 and 97, linked to the golden rule in Article 119(6).

key_cases.subject: Thirty-year rescheduling of municipal financial recovery (Comune di Pagani)
key_cases.holding_en: Intergenerational equity requires not placing a disproportionate burden on future generations' growth opportunities, ensuring sufficient resources for balanced development. Permanent deficit normalisation through legislative deferrals collides with both intra- and intergenerational equity.
key_cases.key_quote_en: Intergenerational equity also requires not placing a disproportionate burden on the growth opportunities of future generations, guaranteeing them sufficient resources for balanced development.
key_cases.significance: First explicit equità intergenerazionale as constitutional review parameter in fiscal law.

key_cases.subject: Multi-year dilution of deficit recovery obligations
key_cases.holding_en: Pluriennial dilution of deficit recovery violates electoral accountability and intergenerational equity; administrators must not leave indefinite financial 'inheritances' to successors.
key_cases.significance: Consolidates 18/2019 line; prelude to 2022 constitutional reform.

key_cases.subject: Abruzzo regional budget; indefinite deficit sanatorie
key_cases.holding_en: Credibility, sustainability, and progressivity of deficit recovery are essential for sound financial management, electoral accountability, and intergenerational equity.

streams.label: Environment, territory, and energy
streams.summary: Post-2022 cases apply Article 9 directly. Environmental derogations must be temporary, proportionate, and aimed at remediation—not permanent lowering of protection standards.

key_cases.subject: Water resources
key_cases.holding_en: Early reference to future generations in resource protection (predates explicit Article 9 reform).

key_cases.subject: Civil uses and collective land domains (usi civici)
key_cases.holding_en: Collective domains are 'inter-generational co-ownership'; future generations cannot be deprived of equal opportunity to use the asset. Diachronic projection ensures environment and landscape for those not yet born.
key_cases.significance: Bridges property/environment law with intergenerational framing before 2022 reform.

key_cases.subject: Government decree on Siracusa petrochemical hub continuity
key_cases.holding_en: First explicit application of reformed Articles 9 and 41. Crisis measures allowing strategic industrial continuity are constitutional only if temporary and aimed at rapid environmental remediation. Court declared unconstitutional the absence of a maximum 36-month operating term.
key_cases.key_quote_en: The perspective of protection indicated by the constitutional legislator extends to the interests of future generations: persons not yet in existence, towards whom present generations owe a duty to preserve environmental conditions.
key_cases.significance: Landmark post-reform environmental constitutional case; 36-month cap read into law.

key_cases.subject: Regional restrictions on renewable energy in parks
key_cases.holding_en: Renewable energy development is of crucial importance for environmental protection including in the interest of future generations; absolute NIMBY bans without ecosystem justification are illegitimate.
key_cases.significance: Balances regional autonomy with national climate/Art. 9 duties.

key_cases.subject: Sardinia regional law on non-suitable areas for FER plants
key_cases.holding_en: Non-suitability cannot mean absolute aprioristic prohibition; retroactive invalidation of authorisations in non-suitable areas violates proportionality and renewable development imperative for future generations.
key_cases.significance: Companion to 134/2025 on renewables vs. regional vetoes.

streams.label: Social solidarity (analogous use)
streams.summary: Uses intergenerational solidarity language in pensions/family law—not environmental doctrine.

key_cases.subject: Survivor pension for same-sex couples married abroad before Law 76/2016
key_cases.holding_en: Reversibility pension as ultrattive family solidarity; exclusion of surviving partner where marriage abroad could not be recognised before partner's death violates equality.
key_cases.significance: Intergenerational chain in pension financing cited, but case is equality/solidarity—not Art. 9 environmental IE.

operational_tests.test: Choices that consume future fiscal space beyond the electoral/budget cycle without correlated benefits are more vulnerable to unconstitutionality.
Derogations from health/environment protection must be proportionate, time-limited, and remediation-oriented—not permanent standard-lowering.
Regional obstacles to renewables face stricter scrutiny when they conflict with Article 9 and decarbonisation imperatives.

vig_framework.english_name: Measures for regulatory simplification and improvement of regulatory quality
vig_framework.statutory_principle: The laws of the Republic promote intergenerational equity also in the interest of future generations (Art. 4(1)).
vig_framework.definition: Generational Impact Assessment (VIG) is a preventive, informational analysis of government normative acts (excluding decree-laws) on environmental or social effects on young people and future generations, with particular attention to intergenerational equity.
vig_framework.integration: VIG is conducted within Regulatory Impact Analysis (AIR) under Law 246/2005.
vig_framework.trigger: Mandatory when a government act has significant environmental or social effects on younger generations and future generations.
exclusions: Decree-laws (decreti-legge) — structural loophole given volume of urgent legislation

institutions.name: National Observatory for Generational Impact of Laws
institutions.location: Presidency of the Council of Ministers
functions: Proposals for tools to define and implement Art. 4 objectives
institutions.resources: Existing staff/budget only; no new public spending; members unpaid

institutions.name: COVIGE (predecessor committee)
institutions.role: Guidelines for generational impact on policies targeting ages 14–35; methodological precursor to VIG

implementing_instruments.deadline: 180 days from Law 167 entry into force (~28 May 2026)
implementing_instruments.concert: Political authority delegated for youth policies
implementing_instruments.status_as_of_2026_06_28: Not located in Gazzetta Ufficiale; ASviS/Save the Children Future Paper (March 2026) treats adoption as pending

art_4_summary: Art. 4(1): Statutory promotion of intergenerational equity
Art. 4(2): VIG definition and scope (government acts, excl. decree-laws)
Art. 4(3): VIG within AIR per DPCM criteria
Art. 4(4): Mandatory VIG for significant environmental/social effects

implementation_status_2026.headline: Legal obligation exists; operational manual still emerging.

provvedimenti.vig_status: Adopted immediately after Law 167 entered force; no published VIG schedule identified; framework described in government focus but not as pilot VIG annex
provvedimenti.note: Primary budget legislation may not have been subject to fully operational VIG methodology

provvedimenti.instrument: Draft delegation law on youth policies and Universal Civic Service (Cabinet approval 22 December 2025)
provvedimenti.vig_status: Pipeline — should embed intergenerational equity per government framing; VIG to be verified in parliamentary passage
provvedimenti.note: Would establish permanent Youth Observatory and National Youth Strategy

provvedimenti.vig_status: Legal duty for significant effects; without DPCM, risk of formalism or inconsistent thresholds
Excluded from mandatory VIG — major implementation gap

future_paper.title: The generational impact assessment of laws: a paradigm shift for public policy

recommendations.text: Treat VIG as permanent cognitive infrastructure for normative design, not a box-ticking exercise.
Shift from defensive (avoid harm) to generative (create opportunities) policy logic.
Embed structured youth and citizen participation in assessments.
Ensure technical independence and adequate resources for Observatory and line ministries.
Strengthen Parliament's capacity to assess intergenerational impact of amendments.
Ensure timeliness — especially for decree-laws (currently excluded).
Promote local VIG and exchange of municipal good practice.
Strengthen national data on childhood, adolescence, and generational transitions.
Build integrated methodological models and indicators.
Include medium/long-term demographic trends in every assessment.

local_practice.detail: VIG integrated into municipal programming (DUP); mandatory labeling of measures as generational / potentially generational / neutral / anti-generational from 2025.
Municipal VIG guidelines adopted May 2024; Brundtland and Agenda 2030 framing.
National guidelines for generational impact assessment in municipal Single Programming Documents (DUP).

comparative_notes.contrast: Institutional commissioner + statutory well-being duties; Italy has constitutional entrenchment + VIG in rulemaking but no national commissioner.
Political intergenerational fairness strategy and Commissioner portfolio; Italy transposes via membership and domestic VIG.
No constitutional future-generations clause; fiscal and youth-governance debate without Art. 9 equivalent.

litigation_track.case: Giudizio Universale (A Sud et al. v. Italy)
litigation_track.relevance: Invoked Art. 9 future generations; procedural barrier not merits.
Corporate climate liability using constitutional future-generations framing.
